claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Mammoth are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kraken are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Kraken win this one.
claims.call: The Kraken keep the Mammoth’s chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot).
claims.nums: Utah 7th for chance quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Seattle 3rd for preventing dangerous shots

chips.tip: Utah: a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, 7th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 10 and 10 games this season.
Seattle: a 6.0% chance of scoring on the average shot against, 3rd of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 10 and 10 games this season.

claims.head: Larsson and Dunn get the Keller assignment
claims.call: The Kraken’s P2 (Larsson and Dunn) spends at least 50% of its 5-on-5 time against the Mammoth’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Kraken keep sending Larsson and Dunn out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Lane Lambert has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Mammoth’s first line is Keller, Schmaltz and Crouse.
claims.nums: At home: 50% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 31% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Lane Lambert likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Mammoth’s first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Seattle home games this season · 3 games, 42 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Seattle’s P2 (Larsson and Dunn) at home: 50% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Seattle home games this season, 3 games, 42 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 31% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: The Mammoth’s power play has a target
claims.call: The Mammoth’s power play creates at least their usual 7.9 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Kraken’s penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Mammoth’s power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Kraken tonight.

notes.text: John Marino is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, up from 2% last season.

SEA.head: The Kraken face a real test
SEA.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Marino, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Kraken can pull it off if they get good looks.

UTA.head: The Mammoth should have the upper hand
UTA.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Marino, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Kraken’s way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Mammoth come in at 7-3-0, the Kraken at 6-3-1.

It’s strength against strength: the Mammoth are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kraken are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Lane Lambert likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Mammoth’s first line.
